questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests release governance, least-privilege principles, and practical DevOps automation in AWS. It also evaluates the ability to translate business requirements into concrete infrastructure changes.

## Key Concepts
- CodePipeline stages and manual approval actions
- Stage-specific artifact storage using separate S3 buckets
- IAM role scoping for production deployments with guardrails

## Code Example
```yaml
Resources:
  ProdPipeline:
    Type: AWS::CodePipeline::Pipeline
    Properties:
      RoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CodePipelineServiceRole
      Stages:
        - Name: Source
          Actions:
            - Name: Source
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Source
                Owner: ThirdParty
                Provider: GitHub
              Configuration:
                Owner: my-org
                Repo: my-repo
                Branch: main
              OutputArtifacts:
                - Name: SourceOutput
        
        - Name: Build
          Actions:
            - Name: Build
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Build
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: CodeBuild
              InputArtifacts:
                - Name: SourceOutput
              OutputArtifacts:
                - Name: BuildOutput
              Configuration:
                ProjectName: MyBuildProject
        
        - Name: Deploy-Staging
          Actions:
            - Name: DeployStaging
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Deploy
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: CloudFormation
              InputArtifacts:
                - Name: BuildOutput
              Configuration:
                StackName: my-app-staging
                TemplatePath: BuildOutput::template.yaml
                RoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CodePipelineDeployRole
              
        - Name: Manual-Approval
          Actions:
            - Name: ApproveProdDeploy
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Approval
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: Manual
              Configuration:
                CustomData: "Please review and approve production deployment"
        
        - Name: Deploy-Production
          Actions:
            - Name: DeployProduction
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Deploy
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: CloudFormation
              InputArtifacts:
                - Name: BuildOutput
              Configuration:
                StackName: my-app-prod
                TemplatePath: BuildOutput::template.yaml
                RoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CodePipelineProdRole
      ArtifactStore:
        Type: S3
        Location: !Ref ProductionArtifactsBucket
  
  StagingArtifactsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: my-app-staging-artifacts
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
  
  ProductionArtifactsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: my-app-production-artifacts
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
  
  CodePipelineProdRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: CodePipelineProdRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: codepipeline.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSCodePipelineFullAccess
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ProductionDeployOnly
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cloudformation:CreateStack
                  - cloudformation:UpdateStack
                  - cloudformation:DeleteStack
                  - cloudformation:DescribeStacks
                Resource: arn:aws:cloudformation:*:*:stack/my-app-prod/*
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:PutObject
                  - s3:ListBucket
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt ProductionArtifactsBucket.Arn
                  - !Sub "${ProductionArtifactsBucket}/*"
              - Effect: Deny
                Action:
                  - cloudformation:CreateStack
                  - cloudformation:UpdateStack
                Resource: arn:aws:cloudformation:*:*:stack/my-app-staging/*
```

## Testing Steps
1. **Pipeline Creation**: Deploy the CloudFormation template and verify the pipeline appears in AWS Console
2. **Artifact Bucket Isolation**: Confirm staging artifacts don't appear in production bucket and vice-versa
3. **Manual Approval**: Trigger the pipeline and verify it stops at the manual approval stage
4. **IAM Guardrails**: Attempt to deploy to staging using the CodePipelineProdRole (should fail)
5. **Production Deployment**: Approve the manual step and verify successful production deployment
6. **Audit Trail**: Check CloudTrail logs for approval actions and deployment events

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes cost-aware, cross-region preview management, tying spend controls to operational gates and rollback readiness. It tests practical implementation details across GitHub Actions, AWS Budgets, and automatic teardown.

## Key Concepts
- Cost governance with per-resource tagging and AWS Budgets
- Ephemeral, multi-region preview environments in EKS
- Idle-resource detection and automated teardown
- Health gates and automated rollback pathways
- Observability and alerting for budget and health events

## Code Example
```yaml
name: cost-aware-preview
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
jobs:
  deploy-preview:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: provision preview
        run: |
          # deploy preview namespaces/clusters via CDK
          npm run cdk deploy PreviewStack -- -c pr_id=${{ github.head_ref }}
      - name: enforce budget tag
        run: |
          # tag resources with pr_id for budgeting
          ./scripts/tag-preview.sh pr_id=${{ github.head_ref }}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate the idle-detection window across regions?
- What changes would you make to handle PR closures vs. merges in budgeting?
